source_standard: Keystone DevRel metrics + DevRel-Qualified-Lead concept (Mary Thengvall) — convergent industry practice, no single ratified standard confirmed (scout-brief gap, stated as assumption); https://openviewpartners.com/blog/measuring-the-impact-of-your-developer-relations-team/ , https://developerrelations.com/talks/measuring-progress-in-developer-relations/

reference_resolution.rule: metric_name must resolve to an actual tracked DevRel metric — no orphan references (issue-515 invariant 2).

recomputation.rule: value is recomputed from the current metric source, never a standalone asserted field.
recomputation.checked_by: TBD (follow-up — issue-521 out-of-scope note: per-role recomputation enforcement is a follow-up once evidence from real usage shows which roles need it)

quality_bar.verification_method: automated check that `product_journey_stage` matches the Keystone stage a metric like this actually measures (awareness = reach/impressions, activation = first successful use, adoption = repeat/sustained use, advocacy = referral/community-contribution signals)
quality_bar.verified_source: OpenView Partners, 'Measuring the Impact of Your Developer Relations Team' — https://openviewpartners.com/blog/measuring-the-impact-of-your-developer-relations-team/ (practitioner-consensus source, not a ratified standard, per the spec's own source_standard note; the awareness/activation/adoption/advocacy funnel is the article's own stated stage taxonomy, matching the spec's `required_fields` enum verbatim).

quality_bar.verification_method: human-review-checklist: does `metric_name` measure a developer behavior change (activation, adoption, advocacy signal) rather than a pure output/vanity count (impressions, follower count) with no behavioral link?
quality_bar.verified_source: Mary Thengvall, 'Measuring Progress in Developer Relations' — https://developerrelations.com/talks/measuring-progress-in-developer-relations/ (practitioner-consensus source, not a ratified standard, per the spec's own source_standard note; the talk's own central argument is that vanity metrics undercount by omitting behavior-linked outcomes).

quality_bar.verification_method: human-review-checklist: for a `product_journey_stage` of adoption or advocacy, does the record name the concrete DevRel-Qualified-Lead criteria used (e.g. repo starred + docs visited + support ticket filed), rather than asserting the stage without a checkable basis?
quality_bar.verified_source: Mary Thengvall, DevRel-Qualified-Lead concept, per OpenView Partners — https://openviewpartners.com/blog/measuring-the-impact-of-your-developer-relations-team/ (practitioner-consensus source, not a ratified standard, per the spec's own source_standard note; DQL is defined there as a named, multi-signal composite, not a single self-asserted claim).

quality_bar.verification_method: automated check that `value` names or links the concrete metric source it was pulled from (analytics dashboard, survey instrument, repo API), matching the spec's own `recomputation` rule that value must be re-derivable from the current metric source
quality_bar.verified_source: OpenView Partners, 'Measuring the Impact of Your Developer Relations Team' — https://openviewpartners.com/blog/measuring-the-impact-of-your-developer-relations-team/ (practitioner-consensus source, not a ratified standard, per the spec's own source_standard note; the article's own repeated critique of DevRel measurement is untraceable self-reported numbers).

quality_bar.verification_method: gates/quality_bar.py:human_comprehensibility_verdict against the role's own docs/issue-<n>/reports/<role>.md record text (gates/human_comprehensibility.py tier-1 structural prose rules: lead paragraph present, citation trailing placement, section size bound, no raw dump, enumeration cap); a record with no human-facing prose section anywhere is exempt (bar-met) -- issue #1623.

use_when.board_condition: a DevRel campaign or content piece ships AND no devrel record exists yet for that campaign
